headline: Stocks Brace for the Open After Thursday's Rout Erased the Post-Election Gains
body_html:
U.S. stocks face Friday's session after a punishing Thursday that, by recent reports, pushed the Nasdaq into correction territory and wiped out the postelection rally. Of the 524 stocks we track, just 45 rose on Thursday while 477 fell, a lopsided tally that leaves the opening tone fragile.

Chips took the brunt. Our semiconductor group dropped 11.99% on average, with Sandisk down 22.26% and MaxLinear down 22.06%. Industrials fell 4.74%, energy and materials 4.22% each, consumer 3.9%, software 2.99% and healthcare 2.15%. Homebuilders, off 1.16%, held up best. Dutch Bros sank 21.41%, while ADMA Biologics gained 26.05% and EPAM Systems 20.63% against the tide.

At the open, watch whether forced selling continues; retail investors reportedly dumped more stocks in a single day than at any point since the Covid sell-off. Crude is headed for a sharp weekly decline, though Middle East supply worries offer a floor, and Iran's reported nuclear proposal sent to Washington through Qatar is a headline risk. Pre-market prices are thin, so treat early moves cautiously.

briefs.headline: Crude Eyes a Steep Weekly Slide
briefs.body: Oil is on track for a sharp weekly drop as signs of oversupply emerge and elevated prices weigh on demand. Lingering supply worries in the Middle East are providing a floor, so the open may show whether buyers defend that level.

briefs.headline: Tehran Reportedly Floats Nuclear Offer via Qatar
briefs.body: A senior Iranian official says a nuclear proposal was passed to the United States through Qatari channels. Any Washington response is a potential catalyst for energy and defense-sensitive names, and markets will be sensitive to the tone of diplomacy.

briefs.headline: ConocoPhillips Lifts Its Payout
briefs.body: The oil producer raised its dividend after quarterly results beat forecasts, helped by higher crude prices. With oil now heading for a weekly decline, investors will weigh whether strong earnings can offset a softer commodity backdrop for the sector.

briefs.headline: Retail Investors Sell at a Pandemic-Era Pace
briefs.body: Individual traders reportedly unloaded more stocks in one day than at any time since the Covid sell-off. Such capitulation can mark exhaustion, but it can also signal further stress, so the opening hour's volume will be closely watched.

briefs.headline: Nasdaq in Correction: History Offers Clues, Not Guarantees
briefs.body: With the tech-heavy index reportedly in correction territory, analysts are revisiting what usually follows such drops. Past episodes vary widely, and the postelection rally's quick reversal leaves traders looking for signs that selling pressure is fading.

briefs.headline: Chip Stocks Lead a Broad Retreat
briefs.body: Semiconductors were the weakest group we track on Thursday, falling 11.99% on average. Sandisk and MaxLinear each shed more than 22%. The open will show whether the group stabilizes or whether the pressure spills further into other technology shares.
